'''Kétévi Adiklè Assamagan''' is an African American physicist at the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]]. He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2021. Assamagan founded the African School of Physics.

== Early life and education ==
Assamagan was born in Port-Gentil [[Gabon]], and moved to [[Togo]] at the age of 4.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Feder |first=Toni |date=2020-10-22 |title=Black voices in physics: Kétévi Assamagan |journal=Physics Today |language=EN |volume=2020 |issue=4 |doi=10.1063/PT.6.4.20201022g |bibcode=2020PhT..2020V1022. |s2cid=243698654}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Meet Kétévi Assamagan, Physicist and Explorer|url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=212044|access-date=2021-10-13|website=Brookhaven National Laboratory|language=en}}</ref> He was an undergraduate student at the [[University of Lomé]].<ref name=":0" /> After earning his bachelor's degree in Physics and Chemistry he was awarded a scholarship from the [[African-American Institute (Northeastern University)|African-American Institute]] to study in the [[United States]], where he joined the [[Southern Illinois University]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Ketevi Assamagan's Biography|url=https://www.thehistorymakers.org/biography/ketevi-assamagan|access-date=2021-10-13|website=The HistoryMakers|language=en}}</ref> He eventually started a graduate studies at [[Ball State University]]. His Master's research involved the development of a two-dimensional analytical model of a solar concentrator.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Two-dimensional analytical model of an n+-p-p+ concentrator solar cell|date=1989|language=English|first=Ketevi Adikle|last=Assamagan|oclc=21010570}}</ref> After earning his master's degree, he moved to the [[University of Virginia]], where he worked toward a doctorate in particle physics.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite thesis|title=A precise determination of the pion beta decay rate: design and calibration|date=1995|language=English|first=Kétévi Adiklè|last=Assamagan|oclc=34689735}}</ref> During his doctorate he worked at the [[Paul Scherrer Institute]].{{citation needed|date=October 2021}}

== Research and career ==
Assamagan was appointed to [[Hampton University]] where he worked on the [[Continuous Electron Beam Accelerator Facility]]. He eventually moved to the [[ATLAS experiment]] in [[CERN]]. His research considers physics beyond the [[Standard Model]].<ref name=":0" /> He moved to [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] in 2001, where he worked on the physics analysis tools for [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS]]. He was made coordinator for the software of the Muon Spectrometer. He was part of the ATLAS Collaboration when they first observed the [[Higgs boson]] in 2012.{{citation needed|date=October 2021}}

Assamagan is co-founder of the African School of Physics,<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Ketevi Assamagan {{!}} The AAS|url=https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/ketevi-assamagan#:~:text=www.africanschoolofphysics.org|access-date=2021-10-13|website=www.aasciences.africa|archive-date=2021-10-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028165232/https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/ketevi-assamagan#:~:text=www.africanschoolofphysics.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Fore|first=Meredith|title=Building up the African physics community|url=https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/building-up-the-african-physics-community|access-date=2021-10-13|website=symmetry magazine|date=21 November 2019 |language=en}}</ref> a non-profit school training African researchers in fundamental physics and applications. In 2019, he co-funded with [[Faïrouz Malek|Fairouz Malek]], Simon Connel and others, the African Strategy for Fundamental Physics.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Crowell |first=Rachel |title=A collective strategy for physics in Africa |work=Symmetry Magazine |url=https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/a-collective-strategy-for-physics-in-africa |access-date=2022-12-26}}</ref> He was elected to the [[African Academy of Sciences]] in 2019 and the [[American Physical Society]] in 2021.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm|access-date=2021-10-13|website=www.aps.org|language=en}}</ref>
